config_name: Legion 5 Gen 10 15.1 — Ryzen AI 7 350 / RTX 5070 8GB (115W), 16GB DDR5, 1TB SSD, 15.1" IPS 165Hz

specs.cpu: AMD Ryzen AI 7 350 (Zen 5 mobile, 8c/16t, 50 TOPS NPU)
specs.gpu: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Laptop 8GB GDDR7 (115 W TGP incl. Dynamic Boost, MUX, no Advanced Optimus)
specs.ports: USB-C 3.2 Gen2 + USB4 40Gbps (DP, PD 3.0), 3x USB-A 3.2, HDMI 2.1, RJ45 GbE, 3.5mm

battery.notes: 80 Wh. NBC measured ~9.5h WiFi @150nits on the AMD Ryzen 7 260 config of this chassis; Ryzen AI 7 350 similar class. ~1h under load; 80% charge in ~52 min.

price.notes: Regular $3,433.99 / sale $2,429.99, BBY API-verified 2026-11-24 (LEGION_LIST.md). Standout sale value: full-TGP RTX 5070 under $2,500.

offers.name: Lenovo Legion 5 Gen 10 15.1" 165Hz Gaming Laptop - Ryzen AI 7 350 - 16GB - 1TB SSD - GeForce RTX 5070 8GB - Eclipse Black

reviews.quote: Lenovo's Legion 5 15 is a very good mainstream gamer, which does not reveal any major issues in our review. The chassis is functional with sufficient ports, a very comfortable keyboard, as well as very good maintenance options.

professional.note: No pro review found for this exact IPS config (honest disclosure per SHARED-legion5-ips.md); the NBC AMD 15AHP G10 review (87%) is the same chassis/CPU class with the OLED panel and RTX 5060. Ratings inferred, disclosed.

praises: At the sale price this is the value pick of the Legion line: full 115W RTX 5070 — NBC says the 5070's gaming is 'on par with the more expensive Legion 5 Pro 16'
AMD Ryzen AI 7 350 keeps battery far above the Intel HX tiers (NBC: AMD ~9.5h WiFi vs 'noticeably shorter' on Intel) and adds a 50 TOPS NPU
IPS panel: no PWM flicker (an NBC con of the OLED sibling) and matte anti-glare at ~500 nits — better in bright rooms than the glossy OLED
AMD model keeps USB4 40Gbps (DP1.4 + PD) that the Intel 5i models lack (NBC ports section)
Best-in-class maintenance: 2x SODIMM to 64GB, 2x M.2, screwed battery, official Lenovo maintenance manual
complaints: 16GB RAM at this price — first upgrade you'll want; 32GB matches what NBC tested
IPS panel lacks OLED's contrast/HDR punch (no 1000-nit HDR, ~1200:1 contrast) — buyers comparing showrooms may prefer the OLED sibling
Fans clearly audible in Performance mode gaming (~50 dB(A) measured on the chassis); quiet at idle though
No card reader; speakers 'could be better' (NBC cons)
Legion Gen-10 platform threads report occasional nvlddmkm TDR driver crashes on some 50-series units and warranty/LENOVEO service friction

standouts: Best sale price-per-gaming-FPS in the Legion 5 lineup ($2,430 for a full-TGP RTX 5070)
AMD efficiency + flicker-free matte IPS = the best battery-and-comfort combo of the non-OLED tiers
design_philosophy: The AMD tier of Lenovo's mainstream Legion 5 Gen 10: full-TGP Blackwell graphics, an efficient Zen 5 CPU with NPU, and easy user maintenance in a restrained chassis. With the matte IPS panel it deliberately trades the OLED's contrast for brightness, no flicker, and a lower price — the pragmatic gamer's config.
rating_notes: Ratings inferred from NBC-reviewed AMD Legion 5 15AHP G10 (87%) and Intel 15IRX10/RTX 5070 (87%) per SHARED-legion5-oled.md + IPS deltas from SHARED-legion5-ips.md: 500-nit 100%sRGB IPS -> screen_quality 6.3, readability_dark 6.8 (no PWM), readability_bright 7.0 (anti-glare beats glossy OLED); Ryzen AI 7 350 (8c Zen5) -> productivity 7.8, battery 8.0 (NBC AMD anchor); RTX 5070 115W -> gaming 7.5; 16GB -> productivity -0.5 / ai_ml -0.3 vs tested 32GB; AMD chassis keeps USB4 -> port_connectivity 7.3.
